q: How much of the 3.6% -> 2.7% IBM-baseline drift is due to FakeHanoi backend-properties refresh vs a genuine modeling choice we mis-reproduced?
basis: Both the released VQE_sim_IBM.p (2.887% at R_opt=0.75 A) and our fresh AerSimulator/FakeHanoiV2 rerun (2.662%) sit visibly below the paper text's stated ~3.6% baseline. Since the released pickle presumably came from the same code the paper reports, the 0.7pp paper-text-vs-released-artifact gap suggests the paper number was generated from an older FakeHanoi snapshot before qiskit-ibm-runtime refreshed the backend properties.
next_steps: Git-blame the FakeHanoi snapshot history in qiskit-terra (pre-v2) and qiskit-ibm-runtime.fake_provider (v2+); pin qiskit-terra==0.44.0 in a clean venv and rerun with the original FakeHanoi (v1); compare per-gate error rates in FakeHanoi across releases; if the drift is confirmed, contact authors to publish a pinned reproducibility environment (Docker image + Zenodo).

q: Would fully independently regenerating the NM curve (rerunning SchWARMA Monte-Carlo trajectories from optimal_schwarma_params.p, not just loading VQE_sim_NM.p) yield the same 0.507% at R_opt, or would per-trajectory variance shift it appreciably?
basis: The 0.507% number is currently derived from the released NM pickle, not from an independent regeneration. Notebook cell 18 is commented out and requires the mezze package (JHU APL internal, not on PyPI or public GitHub). With only 100 MC trajectories, per-seed variance in the SchWARMA-generated beta(t) trajectories could plausibly shift the mean energy by 0.05-0.2pp, comparable to the paper's headline precision.
next_steps: Request mezze from the authors (gregory.quiroz@jhuapl.edu) or reimplement SimpleDephasingSchWARMAFier from the SchWARMA paper (Schultz et al. 2020) directly; rerun with num_MC=100, 500, 1000 to bootstrap a 95% CI on the NM rel-err at R_opt; test whether the 0.5% claim is a point estimate or a mean +- s.e.m.

q: How does the sevenfold advantage scale with circuit depth and qubit count?
basis: The H2 VQE ansatz used for the headline claim has only 2 qubits, 5 single-qubit gates, and 2 CNOTs (depth ~9). Whether a 4-qubit BeH2 or 6-qubit LiH VQE, or a Trotterized dynamics simulation with 20-100 CNOTs, would retain a 5-7x advantage is not addressed. The paper's own multi-qubit DD demonstration (Fig 8) has depth up to 1176 XY4 cycles but is a purely characterizing sequence, not a VQE.
next_steps: Extend the released code to 4-qubit UCCSD H4 or 6-qubit BeH2 with equivalent characterization on a modern IBM Heron device; compare NM-vs-IBM-baseline rel-err at optimal geometries and along dissociation curves; run a depth-vs-fold-improvement scaling study by prepending identity blocks of increasing length.

q: Is the SchWARMA-captured 'correlated dephasing' contribution the same physics as slow 1/f flux noise, or does it also fold in classical control-line noise that would be independently characterizable via cryogenic cabling measurements?
basis: The paper parameterizes correlated dephasing via a fitted SchWARMA (b_hat, a_hat) ARMA filter shaped to the FTTPS-reconstructed dephasing PSD S_beta(omega), without decomposing into microphysical noise sources. The paper's own 'Markovianized' ablation (removing the correlated-dephasing term) collapses NM back to ~3.8% (IBM-parity), showing correlated dephasing IS the key ingredient; but the physical origin remains ambiguous.
next_steps: Compare the fitted S_beta(omega) shape to (a) 1/f^alpha with fitted alpha; (b) known cryo-cabling noise spectra measured on IBMQ devices (Yan et al. flux-qubit references); (c) a Lorentzian-plus-1/f model that separates TLS-like and cabling-like components. Correlate reconstructed PSDs across the 7 devices in Table II with device generation and Josephson-junction fabrication batch.

q: Would this sparse-LME + SchWARMA method retain accuracy on IBM's newer Falcon-r10 / Heron / Eagle-r3 processors, or is the specific parameter set specific to the older Falcon r5/r8 devices used in the paper?
basis: All seven characterized devices (ibm_algiers, ibm_cairo, ibm_hanoi, ibm_lagos, ibmq_belem, ibmq_guadalupe, ibmq_lima) are Falcon-generation (r5.x, r8) or ibmq_pino-generation, all now retired or in-retirement as of 2026. Heron devices use tunable couplers with fundamentally different crosstalk mechanisms (ZZ suppression), so the epsilon, zeta, ZZ crosstalk J parameters in Table I may not transfer.
next_steps: Rerun the full characterization protocol (Table I, ~8 experiment classes) on a current Heron device (ibm_torino, ibm_marrakesh) and refit; test whether the model class remains predictive without adding new terms, or whether a tunable-coupler term must be added; publish a Heron-era supplementary Zenodo release.
